macro.headline: Bull regime intact, but momentum stalling as commodities crack and dollar firms.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY sits at 746.77, up 1.8% over 5 days but down 1.0% over 21 days, above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages, with RSI at a middling 55.6. QQQ mirrors the picture (+3.2% 5d, RSI 56.8). Under the hood, however, MACD histograms on SPY, QQQ and Nasdaq have all rolled negative even while price stays above trend — the classic 'trend up, momentum fading' setup. VIX is contained at 16.74 (-10% over 5d) and the Dow (RSI 65) and Russell 2000 (RSI 64, +3.6% 21d) are actually leading, which is unusual leadership for a tape supposedly driven by mega-cap AI. Meanwhile commodities are in outright retreat: Gold -9.7% over 21 days (RSI 35.6), Silver -21% (RSI 33), WTI crude -25% (RSI 28.9 — deeply oversold), and DXY has ripped +2.2% over 21 days to an overbought RSI of 69. The 10y-2y spread has collapsed 41% over 21 days to just +0.27.

On the causal 'why', the tracked conversation leans bullish 4-to-1 today, with 41 posts. The prevailing sentiment attributes the equity bid to two threads: (1) an AI-infrastructure story anchored on META building out a cloud/AI-compute business to compete with the hyperscalers, and (2) monetary tailwinds — the tracked conversation is flagging a record +$247.8B monthly surge in US M2 money supply as fuel for risk assets. The lone bearish voice is focused on bitcoin's break below $58k on levered liquidations, not equities. Sentiment also attributes gold weakness to record ETF outflows (-38.3 tonnes last week) even as central-bank demand narrative is cited as a longer-term floor — an interesting internal tension. This is broadly consistent with the price data: DXY strength plus commodity weakness aligns with the validated dollar-metals inverse edge, and equity resilience aligns with the M2/AI-capex narrative. However, sentiment does NOT explain the negative MACD histograms across the major indices or the yield-curve compression — those are silent in today's pulse. No clear attribution in today's tracked sentiment for the momentum divergence beneath the surface.

Sector-wise, the rotation tells a defensive-cyclical hybrid story: Healthcare (score 9.8), Industrials (9.2), Russell 2000 (9.2) and Utilities (8.2) are HOT, while Technology and Financials are only 'qualifying' with MACD already bearish. Energy (RSI 34), Communication Services (RSI 36), Consumer Staples and Real Estate are outright weak. This is not a euphoric tape — it's a rotation tape, and the rotation radar is highlighting Travel Services, Diagnostics & Research and Credit Services as the Early-Runway industries with a validated tailwind.

Forward watch: if MACD histograms turn back positive on SPY/QQQ while breadth stays above 55%, the pullback is done and the Early-Runway names are the vehicles. If DXY breaks above 101.8 and 10y-2y goes flat, expect a wobble — commodities and rate-sensitives get hit harder and even the HOT sectors will need to prove leadership. VIX below 15 with breadth above 65% would flip the context to euphoric-caution; VIX above 20 with breadth breaking below 45% would flip to washout-watch.

DXY at 101.41 with RSI 70.6 sits above both its 21d and 50d SMAs, and the backtested DXY_METALS_TAG signal is ACTIVE — an inverse correlation of -0.45 that has held in 70% of rolling 24-month windows. That single vector explains Gold -9.8% on 21d, Silver -21.5%, Oil -25%, and Copper -5.9% all in the same window, while equities chop sideways in a transitional regime.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop cooperates with — rather than fights — the dollar spine. Regime is CHOPPY (confidence 6/10, transitional vote), VIX is 16.67 in contango with VIX3M at 20.13 (no stress bid), and SPY sits mid-band with RSI 55.6 — a trend posture, not a fade setup (per our RSI rule, no overbought-fade edge). Same discipline on Gold/Silver: with DXY still bid, do not front-run a reversal.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is rotating into cyclical/defensive-cyclical hybrids that are dollar-neutral rather than dollar-exposed. XLI +7.2% and XLV +6.6% lead on 21d, XLF +4.3% follows, and IWM +3.7% shows small-caps participating — a healthier internal tape than the headlines suggest. XLK and QQQ are flat on 21d despite XLK's ACCELERATING_BULLISH trajectory vs 50SMA (+7.5%), meaning tech is digesting, not breaking. Rotation flows point into Consumer Electronics, Software-Infrastructure, and unmapped names; nothing is rotating out with conviction, but the fading themes — Precious Metals and Broad Commodity/Ag reflation — are the direct casualties of the dollar spine.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** Semiconductors are the textbook "already run" bucket: HOT 13 months, +258% — a record-tying spell that flags CEILING territory. Manage exits, don't chase entries. The in-range work is elsewhere. Software-Infrastructure is only 1 month into a heat spell (typical 7) with just +3% clocked and FTNT coiling at 94% with bullish flow — early-innings setup. Credit Services shows MA (coil 85.7%, bullish flow) and SOFI (coil 70.9%, bullish flow) as un-run names in a 1-month-young heat spell. Medical Care Facilities (HOT 8 mo, +43%) is extended but still trending; the cleaner risk/reward is in the coiled Software-Infra and Credit Services names, not the semis victory lap.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** DXY 101.80 is the tripwire. A decisive break above confirms the dollar spine and extends pressure on metals, oil, and any dollar-sensitive earner; a rejection back below 99.38 support would be the first real crack, and that's when Gold's RSI 35 / Silver's RSI 32.5 washout would become tradeable rather than a falling knife — but remember, 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days, so even a bounce is not "the low."
